candidate_policy.observed_text:
For the outer-race teaching scenario, the linked NSK example (as commonly presented in NSK bearing-damage education) concerns a deep-groove ball bearing in which the outer ring shows a wear/fretting-type mark, attributed in the example to an operating circumstance such as external vibration while the bearing is stationary (standstill), producing repeated small relative motion at the rolling-contact interface. The general mechanism is contact wear (fretting/ false brinelling): under small oscillatory relative motion between rolling elements and raceway with inadequate or disrupted lubricant film, asperity contact and micro-slip remove or displace material, leaving dull worn or fretted bands at the ball/raceway contact positions. A lubrication-related alternative explanation is that inadequate lubricant quantity, wrong or degraded lubricant, or loss of film (e.g., poor replenishment, contamination, or unsuitable grease for the duty) can produce similar contact-wear or wear marks without any external-vibration cause. The supplied class 'outer_race' is only a caller-assigned teaching label; it establishes no actual cause, no damage mechanism, and no maintenance, reuse, or airworthiness conclusion. The scenario's 'external vibration during standstill' is an independently specified teaching assumption, not an observation or classifier inference.
